I have farmed this land for 40 years. I only finished primary school, but I know my 34.1 mu better than any book. I grow wheat in winter and maize in summer, wheat-maize rotation, always have. My household has seven people, some work in the city and send money back, but the farm still has to pay for itself. I have a well, so I can irrigate when I need to.

For wheat this year, I will do what I did last year. Last year I got about 500 kg per mu, which was fine. I buy improved wheat seed from the dealer, 15 kg per mu, the kind that Lao Wang across the road uses. After the maize comes out in early June, I hire the rotary tiller to chop the stover and turn the soil. Then I plant. For fertilizer, I spread one bag of compound fertilizer 15-15-15 per mu as base—that is 50 kg per mu, so 7.5 kg of nitrogen, phosphorus, and potassium each. Then in March when the wheat turns green, I spread another 25 kg of urea per mu, which gives another 11.5 kg of nitrogen. So in total the wheat gets 19 kg of nitrogen, 7.5 kg of phosphorus, and 7.5 kg of potassium per mu. I irrigate three times: once in winter so the wheat does not freeze to death, once at jointing when it shoots up, and once when the grain fills. I spray herbicide once in spring when the weeds come up, and fungicide once before flowering, so two pesticide sprays total. I would rather spend the money on fertilizer than risk a bad harvest. A bad harvest is a disaster; wasting half a bag of urea is just a cost.

For maize, I plant right after wheat harvest in June. There is no time to waste. I hire a no-till seeder because the soil is still wet and I must plant fast. I use hybrid seed, Zhengdan 958, 2 kg per mu. When planting, I put 25 kg of compound fertilizer 15-15-15 per mu in the row—that is 3.75 kg of nitrogen, phosphorus, and potassium each. Then when the corn is knee-high, about 30 days later, I spread 25 kg of urea per mu, which is another 11.5 kg of nitrogen. So the maize gets 15.25 kg of nitrogen, 3.75 kg of phosphorus, and 3.75 kg of potassium per mu. I irrigate twice: once at planting if June is dry, and once at the big trumpet stage when the tassels come out. If the summer rains are good, maybe I skip one, but I plan for two. I spray herbicide once after planting, and insecticide once when the corn borers appear—two pesticide times. If the weather holds, I expect 600 kg per mu.

I watch my neighbors. If Lao Zhang buys an extra bag of urea this year, I will too. I do not want to be the fool who saved 100 yuan on fertilizer and lost 1,000 yuan on yield. My sons say I should check prices on the internet, but I trust what I see in the field.
